newsitem.title: UK: Dresdner mulls fund mgmt buy in UK - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner mulls fund mgmt buy in UK - paper.

text.p: Germany's Dresdner Bank AG, parent of investment bank Kleinwort Benson, is considering buying another British fund management group, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
"Britain is one of the most interesting markets in asset management," Dresdner director Gerhard Eberstadt was quoted as saying by the paper.

"We are keen to get more mandates in the UK. Our ambitions are not yet satisfied. But as well as wanting to secure more mandates, we are also interested in an acquisition if a reputable firm is available," he said.
Eberstadt said Dresdner might restart talks it held with another fund management group before it bought Kleinwort Benson in 1995.
The report did not disclose the name of the group.

Britain's fund management industry has been in the spotlight recently as a result of fund manager Nicola Horlick's stormy departure from the asset management arm of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, part of Deutsche Bank AG.
Horlick was suspended from the company and later resigned amid accusations she had tried to lure a group of colleagues to leave with her and join rival firm ABN AMRO.
Horlick repeatedly denied the allegations against her. ABN AMRO also denied it tried to poach Horlick's team.
